lessons.title: Find a neutral hand position
lessons.goal: Play low E without gripping the neck or raising the shoulder.
steps: Support the bass with a strap or stable seated position so the fretting hand does not carry its weight.
Pluck open E1 gently, allowing the finger to follow through toward the next thicker-string position or a comfortable rest.
Play four notes then relax both hands for four counts; compare forearm tension before and after without forcing a fixed wrist angle.
lessons.pattern: E1 four quarter notes, then four beats rest
quiz: Place and release notes, not support the instrument's weight

lessons.title: Four tab lines
lessons.goal: Read open-string bass tab from thin G to thick E.
steps: Bass tab's top line is thin G2, followed by D2,A1,E1 downward.
Read one open note on each string: E1-A1-D2-G2, counting four quarter beats.
Write the four zeros on the appropriate lines and play the reverse order; mute each previous string when it should stop.
lessons.pattern: E:0 A:0 D:0 G:0; reverse; quarters

lessons.title: Octaves by ear
lessons.goal: Recognise E1 and E2 as the same note name an octave apart.
steps: Play E1 open string4 and E2 string2 fret2; sing or hum the upper note if the low note is below your comfortable voice.
Hear the same pitch-class identity with a higher register rather than treating both as identical frequency.
Compare E1-A1, a fourth, to E1-E2, an octave; use the interval tool to test distance in an easier vocal register.
lessons.pattern: E1-E2 octave; E1-A1 fourth; compare by listening

lessons.title: A rest is a bass movement
lessons.goal: Silence the string exactly on a one-beat rest.
steps: At 40 BPM play E on1,2,4 and silence3 by lightly touching the string.
Keep counting while muting; do not shorten beat2 because you anticipate the rest.
Repeat on A1 with the same length, then alternate one E bar and one A bar.
lessons.pattern: | E E rest E | A A rest A |; quarter-note beats
quiz: No sounding note while time continues

lessons.title: Original line: Foundation
lessons.goal: Play a two-root groove with controlled note ends.
steps: Bar1 E1 on1 and3, each lasting one beat, with rests on2 and4.
Bar2 A1 on1,2,3, then rest4; mute the previous E string before changing.
Repeat four cycles, listening to space rather than only attacks. Climb the ladder without letting notes cover the rests.
lessons.pattern: | E(1) rest(1) E(1) rest(1) | A A A rest |
quiz: The first bar has how many sounding attacks?

lessons.title: Cross a string without ringing
lessons.goal: Mute the old string when moving to a new one.
steps: Play E1 then A1 slowly, muting E with the thumb or another relaxed finger before A sounds.
Use the fretting hand's light touch on unused thinner strings; do not press them to the fretboard.
Repeat E-A-D-G and back with alternating fingers. Compare the phrase with and without muting to hear unwanted overlap.
lessons.pattern: E A D G D A E; quarter beats, one sounding string at a time
quiz: Lightly damped when not intended to ring
Allowed to drone in every exercise

lessons.title: A small first-position map
lessons.goal: Play E-F-G-A using safe position changes.
steps: Use E1 open string4, F1 fret1, G1 fret3, A1 open string3.
Use fingers1 and4 or a small shift for frets1 and3 if that is more comfortable; low bass frets are widely spaced.
Ascend and descend, naming the half step E-F and whole step F-G; stop rather than force a long reach.
lessons.pattern: E string0,1,3; A string0; reverse

lessons.title: Half and whole notes in a bar
lessons.goal: Hold bass notes for their full written duration.
steps: In 4/4 a half note occupies two quarter beats and a whole note four.
Play E1 for beats1-2, A1 for3-4, then D2 for the next whole bar.
Count while sustaining and release exactly at the next attack; the equal-note reference only checks pitch sequence.

lessons.title: Eight even plucks
lessons.goal: Alternate fingers on eight equal eighth notes.
steps: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & at 40 BPM and alternate index-middle on open E.
Keep both fingers equally quiet; an alternating motion is not an alternating loud-soft accent.
Change to A for bar2 without adding time at the string crossing; practise only four attacks at first if necessary.
lessons.pattern: Eight E eighths per bar, then eight A eighths; i-m alternation

lessons.title: Original line: Engine Room
lessons.goal: Keep an eighth-note rock pulse across two roots.
steps: Bars1-2 use E1 eighths; bars3-4 use A1 eighths.
Make beat1 slightly clearer but avoid pounding the string into the frets.
On the repeat, leave the & of4 silent in each bar; maintain finger alternation through that silent subdivision.
lessons.pattern: E E A A, one bar each; eighths; second take omits4&
quiz: Leave silence without shortening the bar

lessons.title: Release pressure, not the whole hand
lessons.goal: End fretted notes with a controlled light touch.
steps: Play A1 at string4 fret5, then relax finger pressure while retaining light contact to mute.
Alternate A with B1 fret7 using a comfortable shift; avoid reaching through pain.
Compare two-beat sustained notes with one-beat notes followed by rests; make duration a conscious fretting-hand action.
lessons.pattern: E string5(1), rest(1),7(1),rest(1); repeat
quiz: Mute a fretted note without pulling the hand away

lessons.title: C major's first five tones
lessons.goal: Play C-D-E-F-G across two strings.
steps: Use C2 string3 fret3, D2 fret5; E2 string2 fret2, F2 fret3, G2 fret5.
Choose small shifts instead of holding a stretched five-fret position.
Say each pitch before plucking, then sing the contour. Identify E-F as the only semitone in these five notes.
lessons.pattern: A:3,5; D:2,3,5; reverse; one quarter per note

lessons.title: Bass guitar's written octave
lessons.goal: Match sounding E1 with written E2 on the bass staff.
steps: Bass guitar conventionally sounds one octave lower than its written bass-clef notes.
Open E1 appears as written E2 below the staff; open A1 as written A2 in the bottom space.
Play E1-A1-D2-G2 and read their written E2-A2-D3-G3 positions, keeping mic targets in sounding pitch.
lessons.pattern: Sound E1 A1 D2 G2; written E2 A2 D3 G3

lessons.title: Hear major and minor thirds
lessons.goal: Compare C-E and C-Eb to identify chord quality.
steps: Play C2 string3 fret3 then E2 string2 fret2; count four semitones for the major third.
Replace E with Eb2 string2 fret1, a three-semitone minor third.
Make two-note answers while a helper calls major or minor. Bass lines need not play whole chords to reveal their quality.
lessons.pattern: C2-E2 major third; C2-Eb2 minor third

lessons.title: Original line: Note Trail
lessons.goal: Play a melodic bass phrase with a measured ending.
steps: Use | C D E G | F E D C | as quarters in the sounding octave2.
Keep shifts small and mute unused strings; rehearse the two-string crossing separately.
Repeat with final C held two beats by replacing bar2 with F-E-C(2). Write the change rather than adding an uncounted sustain.
lessons.pattern: | C2 D2 E2 G2 | F2 E2 D2 C2 |; optional final C(2)

lessons.title: The root stays in the name
lessons.goal: Follow C, Am, F and G chord symbols with correct roots.
steps: C means root C, Am root A, F root F and G root G; m changes quality, not the root letter.
Find C2 string3 fret3, A1 open3, F1 string4 fret1 and G1 fret3.
Play one whole-note root per bar in C-Am-F-G, naming the upcoming chord before beat1.

lessons.title: Shift before the next root
lessons.goal: Move between roots without a tense reach.
steps: Play G1 fret3 to C2 string3 fret3, then D2 fret5 on that string.
Release pressure briefly during shifts while keeping light muting contact; do not drag a pressed finger loudly unless a slide is intended.
Count four beats per root and plan the move during the release. Rehearse just the last subdivision into beat1.
lessons.pattern: G1-C2-D2-G1, four beats each; planned release and shift
quiz: Relaxed pressure and a planned move
A locked wrist stretched to every fret
An extra beat at each change

lessons.title: A minor five-note home
lessons.goal: Play A-B-C-D-E and hear its minor third.
steps: Use A1 open3, B1 fret2, C2 fret3; D2 open2, E2 fret2.
Play slowly, noting B-C as the half step and A-C as a minor third.
Over an A root, make a short answer ending A or E. Sing before playing to keep the line musical rather than a fret pattern.
lessons.pattern: A:0,2,3; D:0,2; reverse
quiz: The third of A minor is...

lessons.title: Support beats one and three
lessons.goal: Place bass notes with an imagined kick pattern.
steps: Count four beats and tap a foot on every beat without locking the knee.
Play a one-beat root on1 and3, resting2 and4; then hold each note two beats for a longer version.
Compare the short and long grooves over C-Am-F-G. Neither is automatically better; the note lengths should fit the imagined drum part.
lessons.pattern: Roots on1,3 over C-Am-F-G; short then two-beat notes
quiz: Bass note length should respond to...
The musical groove and desired space

lessons.title: Original line: Home Floor
lessons.goal: Build a four-bar root groove with one planned variation.
steps: Use C-Am-F-G, roots on1 and3, with rests2 and4.
On the second cycle add one eighth-note root on4& in bar4 as a pickup into C.
Write the pickup and repeat twice; avoid adding a fill at every change. Confirm the next bar starts exactly on1.
lessons.pattern: C-Am-F-G roots1,3; optional G1 on last4& leading to C2
quiz: A pickup into the next bar must...
Fit before the next beat1 without moving it

lessons.title: G major with one sharp
lessons.goal: Play a G-major octave containing F#.
steps: Use G1 string4 fret3, A1 fret5; B1 string3 fret2, C2 fret3,D2 fret5; E2 string2 fret2,F#2 fret4,G2 fret5.
Move in small comfortable positions and sing the semitone F#-G.
Write F# in the key signature and compare the scale with G natural minor's Bb,Eb,F if you know it; keep this exercise's major notes distinct.
lessons.pattern: E:3,5; A:2,3,5; D:2,4,5; G-major octave

lessons.title: Apply the signature in every octave
lessons.goal: Remember F# throughout a G-major bass line.
steps: In a G-major signature every written F becomes F# unless cancelled.
Play G1-B1-D2-F#2 then G2, using sounding pitches while reading the octave-higher staff.
Write the sequence twice in different octaves and mark any natural sign explicitly; do not assume only the first F is sharp.
lessons.pattern: G1 B1 D2 F#2 G2; signature F#
quiz: F notes in every octave unless cancelled

lessons.title: A natural minor octave
lessons.goal: Play natural minor and identify its flat third and seventh.
steps: A1-B1-C2-D2-E2-F2-G2-A2 uses the C-major note collection with A as home.
Use string3 frets0,2,3; string2 frets0,2,3; string1 frets0,2.
Compare C to C# and G to G# by ear; natural minor keeps C and G natural. Finish a phrase on A.
lessons.pattern: A:0,2,3; D:0,2,3; G:0,2; A natural minor

lessons.title: The third tells the story
lessons.goal: Outline major and minor triads with roots, thirds and fifths.
steps: Play C2-E2-G2 then A1-C2-E2, naming major and minor quality.
Count four beats: root1, third2, fifth3, third4.
Over C-Am-F-G use matching third qualities; F's A is major, G's B is major, Am's C minor.
lessons.pattern: Each bar root-third-fifth-third; C,Am,F,G
quiz: The third over Am should be...

lessons.title: Original line: Key Road
lessons.goal: Transpose a degree-based groove to C and G.
steps: Use degrees1-3-5-3 as quarters followed by2-4-5-1 in the next bar.
Play in C first, then G with F# available if you add degree7.
Write both pitch lists and compare the interval contour. Keep the same durations while changing the home pitch.
lessons.pattern: G: | G1 B1 D2 B1 | A1 C2 D2 G1 |; also transpose to C
quiz: Retaining interval roles around a new root

lessons.title: A two-beat root-fifth feel
lessons.goal: Place root on one and fifth on three with even releases.
steps: Over C use C2 string3 fret3 on1 and G1 string4 fret3 on3, each held two beats.
For F use F1 fret1 and C2 fret3; for G use G1 fret3 and D2 string2 open.
Repeat C-F-G-C and listen to the fifth below as an alternative to above. Keep four beats per bar even if only two notes sound.
quiz: Above or below the root in register

lessons.title: Fifth and sixth shuffle motion
lessons.goal: Alternate E's fifth and sixth as a blues accompaniment.
steps: Play E1 root then B1 fifth string3 fret2, then E1 and C#2 sixth fret4.
Use small shifts rather than holding an extended reach; add light damping to define the groove.
Play long-short pairs using the first and third triplet subdivisions. The added sixth is a line colour, not a change of root.
lessons.pattern: E-B, E-C# long-short pairs; fifth/sixth shuffle

lessons.title: Twelve-bar root roadmap
lessons.goal: Track a twelve-bar E blues form.
steps: Write E7 for1-4, A7 for5-6, E7 for7-8, B7 for9, A7 for10, E7 for11, B7 for12.
Play roots E1,A1,B1 for four beats each, calling bar numbers aloud.
Add fifths only after the roadmap stays secure. Use your own metronome; the built-in C-F-G-C backing is not an E blues.
lessons.pattern: 12 bars E E E E A A E E B A E B; dominant-seventh harmony

lessons.title: E-minor blues fragment
lessons.goal: Use G-A-Bb-B as a controlled blues colour.
steps: E minor blues is E-G-A-Bb-B-D-E.
Use E1 open4,G1 fret3; A1 open3,Bb1 fret1,B1 fret2; D2 open2,E2 fret2.
Make a short phrase in which Bb passes into B, then stop on E. Hear the tension rather than making every chromatic note equal.
lessons.pattern: E:0,3; A:0,1,2; D:0,2; E minor blues
quiz: The passing blues tone between A and B is...

lessons.title: Original line: Dirt Road
lessons.goal: Play a twelve-bar shuffle with one measured turnaround.
steps: Use the printed E-blues form, alternating root and fifth as long-short pairs.
In bar12 play B1-D2-D#2-E2 as quarters to approach the next E root; identify D# as a chromatic leading tone rather than an E-minor scale tone.
Perform roots only once, then the full line twice. Simplify the turnaround if it moves the next beat1.
lessons.pattern: 12-bar E blues; root/fifth shuffle; bar12 B-D-D#-E quarters
quiz: The D# in the turnaround functions as...

lessons.title: Hold an offbeat over one
lessons.goal: Sustain a bass pickup across the next downbeat.
steps: Count1&2&3&4& and play E1 only on4&.
Tie through the next beat1, release on2, then play G1 on3 and E1 on4.
Tap the downbeat with a foot while the hand does not re-attack. Clap only sounding attacks before plucking.
lessons.pattern: E on4& tied through next1; rest2; G on3,E on4
quiz: Sustain without a new downbeat pluck

lessons.title: A deliberate dead note
lessons.goal: Create a light percussive note without an unintended pitch.
steps: Rest fretting fingers lightly across a string without pressing to a fret; pluck softly to produce a short x sound.
Compare muted x with pitched E1; the muted event is rhythm, not a target note for the pitch detector.
Play E-x-E-rest as quarters. Keep the hand relaxed and do not strike so hard that the bass rattles or fingers hurt.
lessons.pattern: | E1 x E1 rest |; x is an unpitched self-assessed event
quiz: A dead note should be assessed for...
Rhythm and damping, not a definite pitch

lessons.title: A-minor pentatonic pocket
lessons.goal: Use A-C-D-E-G in a compact groove.
steps: Find A1 open3,C2 fret3,D2 open2,E2 fret2,G2 open1.
Play ascending slowly, then make a three-note answer A-C-E with a beat of silence.
Move the answer's first attack to1& while retaining chord-tone A on the next bar1. Record weak rhythm separately from pitch errors.
lessons.pattern: A C D E G; phrase A-C-E then rest; optional1& entrance
quiz: B and F from A natural minor

lessons.title: Four slots in each beat
lessons.goal: Count sixteenth-note positions before adding speed.
steps: Say1 e & a,2 e & a at40 BPM; clap all subdivisions first.
Play E only on1 and1a, then2&; repeat the two-beat cell with rests in other slots.
Keep the click on quarter beats. Use muted taps first if plucking every subdivision makes the fingers tighten.
lessons.pattern: Two-beat cell: E on1,1a,2&; rest all other sixteenth slots
quiz: The fourth sixteenth subdivision of beat1

lessons.title: Original line: Side Street
lessons.goal: Combine syncopated notes, a dead note and written rests.
steps: Bar1 E1 on1, x on2, E1 on2&, G1 on3&, E1 on4; all attacks short.
Bar2 A1 on1 and2&, C2 on3, E2 on4& as pickup; count the empty slots.
Repeat two bars with consistent dynamics. The pitch reference omits x and rests, so judge actual timing yourself.
lessons.pattern: | E1 x2 E2& G3& E4 | A1 A2& C3 E4& |; numbers denote beat placements
quiz: The pitch reference can grade the dead note's timing?
No, rhythm and dead notes are self-assessed

lessons.title: Read low ledger positions
lessons.goal: Distinguish written E2, G2, B2 and D3.
steps: Bass-clef bottom line is G2; E2 sits on the ledger line below, B2 on the second line, D3 on the middle line.
For bass guitar these sound E1,G1,B1,D2; map each to an open or fretted position.
Play E1-G1-B1-D2 and cover pitch labels on paper. Read contour and letter spacing, not only fret numbers.
lessons.pattern: Sounding E1 G1 B1 D2; written E2 G2 B2 D3

lessons.title: F major and Bb
lessons.goal: Play F major with an accurate flat fourth.
steps: Use F1 string4 fret1,G1 fret3,A1 fret5; Bb1 string3 fret1,C2 fret3,D2 fret5; E2 string2 fret2,F2 fret3.
Shift as needed instead of spanning frets1-5 continuously.
Sing A-Bb to hear the semitone and end a short phrase on F. Write Bb in the signature, noting the display uses A# enharmonically.
lessons.pattern: F G A Bb C D E F; planned position shifts

lessons.title: Choose lengths to support a singer
lessons.goal: Control long and short bass articulations intentionally.
steps: Play four C2 quarters very short, then four with almost full-beat sustain.
Sing a slow melody while alternating the bass versions; notice which note length leaves more room.
Write a two-bar mix of short quarters and half-note sustains. Use both hands' muting to shape endings, not random loss of pressure.
lessons.pattern: C2 four short quarters; four sustained quarters; same BPM
quiz: Attack/release character without changing the written beat count

lessons.title: Anticipate the next root
lessons.goal: Place an upcoming chord root on4& without losing the form.
steps: Over C-F-G-C play roots on1 and3 first.
Then introduce the next bar's root on the current4&, tied through the next1.
Name both the current and upcoming harmony before playing; do not move the entire chord progression early without musical intent.
lessons.pattern: C-F-G-C; next root on4&, tied over next1
quiz: An upcoming harmony's note before its downbeat
A random note unrelated to the next chord

lessons.title: Original line: Soft Landing
lessons.goal: Read a four-bar line with ties and different note lengths.
steps: Clap attacks and sustain counts before adding bass. The offbeat G connects bars2 and3.
Play twice with a quieter final C; explain why the tie avoids another attack at bar3 beat1.
lessons.pattern: 4/4 C-F-G-C; offbeat G tied into bar3; final C whole note

lessons.title: Major, minor and dominant sevenths
lessons.goal: Outline Cmaj7, Dm7 and G7 distinctly.
steps: Cmaj7 tones C-E-G-B, Dm7 D-F-A-C, G7 G-B-D-F; name each quality.
Play one tone per quarter beat in a safe register, shifting rather than forcing wide reaches.
Hear B as Cmaj7's major seventh and F as G7's minor seventh. Compare C7's Bb so the symbols are not confused.
lessons.pattern: Cmaj7 C2-E2-G2-B2; Dm7 D2-F2-A2-C3; G7 G1-B1-D2-F2

lessons.title: Shift through an arpeggio
lessons.goal: Keep arpeggio shifts quiet and in time.
steps: Play C2-E2-G2-C3 using string3 fret3,string2 fret2,string1 fret0 then5.
Rehearse the G2-C3 hand move without sound, then add a brief release that does not leave an extra beat.
Repeat ascending and descending at60 BPM with clean muting. Stop if the wrist bends sharply or a reach becomes painful.
lessons.pattern: A:3; D:2; G:0,5; C-major arpeggio and reverse
quiz: A fixed hand stretch at all costs

lessons.title: Approach a root by semitone
lessons.goal: Use a chromatic approach as a deliberate last-beat tension.
steps: To approach C2 from below, play B1 on beat4 then C2 at next1.
To approach F1, use E1 on4; to approach G1, use F#1.
Write approach notes outside the key as intentional chromatic tones, not incorrect permanent scale changes. Resolve exactly on the next root.
lessons.pattern: B1->C2; E1->F1; F#1->G1; approach on4,root next1
quiz: A chromatic approach succeeds when it...
Resolves intentionally into the target harmony
Is always held for four bars

lessons.title: Read the note after the slash
lessons.goal: Play the specified bass under slash-chord symbols.
steps: C/E asks for E bass under C harmony; C/G asks for G bass. The slash does not mean division.
Play C2-E2-F2-G2 under C-C/E-F-G for four bars.
Distinguish chord root C from actual bass E in bar2 and sing the stepwise bass C-E-F-G contour.
lessons.pattern: | C | C/E | F | G |; bass C2 E2 F2 G2

lessons.title: Original line: Harmonic Route
lessons.goal: Connect ii-V-I arpeggios with purposeful approaches.
steps: Bar1 Dm7 D2-F2-A2-C3; bar2 G7 G1-B1-D2-B1; bar3 Cmaj7 C2-E2-G2-B2; bar4 C2(2),G1(1),C2(1).
The B1 on bar2 beat4 approaches C2 by semitone; keep its resolution precise.
Play twice at the ladder target, then remove one inner note as a rest without losing the four-bar structure.
lessons.pattern: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7; quarter walking arpeggios, last bar2+1+1

lessons.title: Read a four-bar ii-V-I walk
lessons.goal: Keep chord roots on strong downbeats while following a lead sheet.
steps: Write Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7 and number the bars.
Play root-third-fifth-approach with one quarter per beat: D-F-A-F#, G-B-D-B, C-E-G-B, C-G-E-C.
Check that F# is a chromatic approach to G, not a Dm7 chord tone. Count bar numbers while first playing roots only.
lessons.pattern: | D F A F# | G B D B | C E G B | C G E C |
quiz: F# before the G7 bar is...

lessons.title: Quarter-note walking, not shuffle
lessons.goal: Keep walking quarters even under a swung ensemble feel.
steps: Play C2-D2-E2-G2 as even quarters while saying a quiet triplet subdivision.
Walking quarter attacks still align to each beat; do not turn every quarter into a long-short pair.
Add one optional triplet pickup before a bar line only after two plain passes remain stable; keep the pickup quiet and subordinate.
lessons.pattern: | C2 D2 E2 G2 |; four even walking quarters
quiz: A basic walking line usually attacks...
Only the first and third triplet slots

lessons.title: D Dorian for passing motion
lessons.goal: Connect Dm7 tones with a natural sixth colour.
steps: D Dorian is D-E-F-G-A-B-C-D, sharing C-major notes.
Play D-F-A-C first, then fill gaps with E,G,B; B is the natural sixth relative to D.
Compose a quarter-note bar D-F-B-C leading to G7, listening to whether the line supports rather than obscures the harmony.
lessons.pattern: D E F G A B C D; Dm7 anchors D F A C
quiz: D Dorian differs from D natural minor by...

lessons.title: Hear third and seventh resolutions
lessons.goal: Hear F move to E through a G7-C cadence.
steps: Play G1-F2, then C2-E2; F is G7's seventh and E is C's third.
Sing F-E while a helper plays the roots G-C, then choose a bass line containing that movement.
Try D2-F2-G1-F2-C2-E2 and hear the ii-V-I. This is harmonic ear work, not a demand to play all chord tones at once.
lessons.pattern: G7 seventh F -> C third E; ii-V-I guide-tone study

lessons.title: Original line: After Hours
lessons.goal: Write two contrasting walking choruses of a four-bar form.
steps: First chorus use the printed Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7 walk from this unit.
Second chorus keep roots on beat1 and choose different chord tones on2-3 plus a diatonic or chromatic approach on4.
Write every note, check each approach's destination, then perform both choruses without resetting the pulse between them.
lessons.pattern: Two four-bar ii-V-I choruses; root1, chord tones2-3, approach4
quiz: A walking approach is planned around...

lessons.title: Read an attack grid
lessons.goal: Translate a sixteen-slot rhythm grid into counted attacks.
steps: Write four groups1e&a,2e&a,3e&a,4e&a and mark attacks on1,1a,2&,3,3a,4&.
Tap the grid without bass, then play only E1 on those slots.
Replace the second and fifth attacks with muted x; the pitch reference omits unpitched events, so the grid is your timing authority.
lessons.pattern: E on1,2&,3,4&; x on1a,3a; rest remaining slots

lessons.title: Optional light slap and pop
lessons.goal: Explore a percussive bass attack without force.
steps: On your instrument try a small thumb motion near the end of the fingerboard on open E; immediately release so the string can vibrate.
Try a gentle index-finger pop on G without pulling far from the body. Start very softly and stop for pain; conventional fingerstyle is an equally valid alternative.
Alternate an E thumb attack and G pop at half-note spacing; listen for balanced volume. The app does not grade slap timbre.
lessons.pattern: E1(2),G2(2); optional slap/pop or ordinary fingerstyle
quiz: Small comfortable motions and balanced sound

lessons.title: A-minor seventh groove tones
lessons.goal: Use A-C-E-G without confusing the root.
steps: Name Am7 tones A,C,E,G and locate them across strings3-1.
Play A1 on1, C2 on2&, E2 on3, G2 on4&.
Move the last G to A2 as an octave ending on alternate bars; keep chord quality from C rather than substituting C#.
lessons.pattern: Am7 attacks1,2&,3,4&; second bar octave A instead of G

lessons.title: Move a pentatonic cell
lessons.goal: Transpose a minor-pentatonic groove from A to D.
steps: A cell A-C-D-E corresponds to D-F-G-A after transposition.
Play A1-C2-D2-E2, then D2-F2-G2-A2 with the same attack grid.
Say degrees1-b3-4-5, then compare both by ear. Shift hands comfortably before increasing BPM.
lessons.pattern: A C D E -> D F G A; same rhythm1,1a,2&,3
quiz: The minor third above D is...

lessons.title: Original line: Pocket Machine
lessons.goal: Perform a funk cell with exact rests and controlled ghost notes.
steps: Two Am7 bars: A1 on1, x on1a, C2 on2&, E2 on3, x on3a, G2 on4&.
Two Dm7 bars use D2,F2,A2,C3 in the same pitched slots.
Repeat all four bars with consistent attack volume. Demonstrate the groove in fingerstyle first; slap/pop is optional and requires separate timbre self-assessment.
lessons.pattern: Am7 Am7 Dm7 Dm7; pitched1,2&,3,4&; ghost1a,3a

lessons.title: End the fill before the root
lessons.goal: Place a two-beat fill without moving the next downbeat.
steps: Play C2 for two beats, then E2-G2-A2-G2 as eighths on3&4&.
Next bar begins F1 exactly on1; rehearse only the last eighth into F.
Create a different fill but keep the two-beat limit. A fill should support the phrase boundary, not replace the next harmony.
lessons.pattern: C2(2), E2-G2-A2-G2 eighths on3&4&; F1 next1
quiz: A fill's most important destination is...
The next musical downbeat or target
A pause before the next bar

lessons.title: Low foundation, high answer
lessons.goal: Use register contrast without losing the bass role.
steps: Play C2-G1 as low support, then C3-E3-G3 at string1 frets5,9,12 as a higher answer.
Use relaxed shifts and return to C2 before the next chord change; do not force an extended stretch.
Compare a whole chorus low with one containing a single high answer. Ask whether the melody and ensemble still have room.
lessons.pattern: C2-G1 support; C3-E3-G3 answer; return to C2
quiz: High-register fills work best when they...
Have space and return to the line's supporting role

lessons.title: Harmonic minor's raised seventh
lessons.goal: Use G# to lead into A in a minor cadence.
steps: A harmonic minor is A-B-C-D-E-F-G#-A, unlike natural minor's G.
Play E1-G#1-B1-D2 for E7 and resolve to A1-C2-E2.
Use G# briefly before A in a fill; keep C natural for the minor tonic and hear the dominant's major third.
lessons.pattern: A harmonic minor; E7 E-G#-B-D resolves Am A-C-E

lessons.title: Verse, bridge and return
lessons.goal: Follow a twelve-bar A-B-A roadmap with slash bass.
steps: A is four bars C-G/B-Am-F; B is Dm-G-C-C; perform A-B-A.
G/B requires B1 bass while harmony remains G. Write bar numbers and actual bass roots separately.
Play roots only then add one fill before each section return; keep unfilled bars simple enough to hear the form.
lessons.pattern: 12 bars A(C G/B Am F)-B(Dm G C C)-A

lessons.title: Original line: Grounded Story
lessons.goal: Arrange a complete bass part with dynamics and two intentional fills.
steps: Use the previous A-B-A chord roadmap. In first A play roots1,3; in B use root-third-fifth-approach quarters.
In final A return to the simpler groove, adding a two-beat fill only in bar12 leading back to C.
Write the exact notes and rests, choose a dynamic high point in B, and perform two uninterrupted takes. Assess pitch, note lengths, form and supportive groove separately.
lessons.pattern: 12-bar A-B-A; simple verse, walking bridge, restrained return and measured fill
quiz: Form, supportive time, note lengths and intentional harmony
